findings.evidence: Proof body: `(isomorphisms Scheme).of_isPullback h (isomorphisms.infer_property (𝟙 X))`; `Mathlib/CategoryTheory/MorphismProperty/Basic.lean:684` — `theorem isomorphisms.infer_property [hf : IsIso f]`, so the generalization is a one-token change.
findings.fix: State `theorem geometricallyIntegral_of_isIso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : GeometricallyIntegral f`, replacing `isomorphisms.infer_property (𝟙 X)` with `isomorphisms.infer_property f`; derive `geometricallyIntegral_id X := geometricallyIntegral_of_isIso (𝟙 X)` if still wanted.
findings.issue: Under-generalized: the proof never uses that the morphism is `𝟙 X` — it only uses `(isomorphisms Scheme) (𝟙 X)`. The natural statement is for any isomorphism, with the identity a special case.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Geometrically/Integral.lean:66,69,72,75 are all instances; Trivial.lean lines 51-52 mix `inferInstanceAs (IsProper ...)` with the explicit `geometricallyIntegral_id (Spec (.of K))`.
findings.fix: Register it as `instance (priority := low) [IsIso f] : GeometricallyIntegral f` (or a `MorphismProperty.ContainsIdentities @GeometricallyIntegral` instance), letting `Trivial.lean` write `geometricallyIntegral := inferInstance`.
findings.issue: Wrong interface level: every other closure fact for this class in Mathlib is an instance (`instance : IsStableUnderBaseChange @GeometricallyIntegral`, `instance [GeometricallyIntegral g] : GeometricallyIntegral (pullback.fst f g)`, etc.), so downstream code resolves them by `inferInstance`. Here the consumer must pass the term explicitly, asymmetrically with `isProper := inferInstanceAs ...` on the adjacent line.

summary: The trivial abelian variety itself is at the right level, but the supporting lemma `geometricallyIntegral_id` is stated for identities when its own proof establishes the fact for every isomorphism, and it is a plain theorem where Mathlib's surrounding closure facts are instances.
